value.body: An instructional designer plans and builds learning material — school and college course content, corporate training modules and e-learning courses. Ed-tech companies, e-learning firms, publishers and corporate training teams hire for the role.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.A. or Master's in Education or a subject, with writing samples

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Word processors, presentation tools, e-learning authoring tools, LMS platforms

items.label: M.Ed enrolment (all modes)
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 11, actual responses

items.label: SWAYAM online course enrolments (cumulative)
items.note: Government MOOC platform; 14,000+ courses offered so far (as reported)
items.source: UGC notice on SWAYAM (as reported, Careers360)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start as content developers or associate instructional designers, selected through a writing or design assignment; a portfolio of sample lessons helps.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Learning design models (such as ADDIE, Bloom's taxonomy)

value.title: At a glance
items: A background in education theory is directly useful here.
Corporate e-learning and K-12 content are the two main markets.
Growth leads to senior designer, learning experience designer or curriculum lead.

value.title: B.A. B.Ed. (integrated) enrolment
value.note: All modes; based on institutions that responded to AISHE. B.A. B.Ed. is an integrated teacher-education programme; enrolment is not a count of instructional design jobs.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 11, actual responses
